questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  M-mode was the first modality in echocardiography. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: M-mode (motion mode) was the earliest echocardiographic display, predating cross-sectional 2D imaging. Otto traces echo's origins to these single-line motion tracings. *(Practice review slide 3.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What is the sampling rate of M-mode imaging?
questions.explanation: M-mode interrogates a single scan line, so pulses aren't shared across a sector. Sampling reaches roughly 1000–2000 frames/s (≈1800), giving outstanding temporal resolution. *(Practice review slide 5.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  M-mode is the gold standard for measurements. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: Current ASE/Otto guidance favours direct 2D (or 2D-guided) linear measurements. A fixed M-mode cursor often can't stay perpendicular to the walls, which overestimates dimensions. *(Practice review slide 7.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What is a characteristic of M-mode imaging?
options: Gives a visual representation of the anatomy
questions.explanation: M-mode's hallmarks are outstanding temporal resolution and a narrow single-line ‘ice-pick’ sample — so both b and c are correct. *(Practice review slide 9.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Time is represented on the y-axis. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: On an M-mode tracing, time runs along the horizontal X-axis; depth (distance from the transducer) is on the vertical Y-axis. *(Practice review slide 11.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  The cursor needs to be perpendicular to the structure of interest for best practice. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: Perpendicular insonation yields the truest dimension and the strongest specular reflection from walls and valves. *(Practice review slide 13.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Sweep speed can be adjusted on M-mode imaging to adjust for clinical situations and heart rate. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: Sweep speed is an operator-adjustable control that spreads or compresses the trace to suit the patient's heart rate and the event being studied. *(Practice review slide 15.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Where is end-diastole marked on the ECG?
options: At the beginning of the QRS complex
At the peak of the R wave
At the end of the T wave
questions.explanation: By the classic M-mode convention, end-diastole is taken at the peak of the R wave — the onset of ventricular contraction, when the LV is maximally filled. *(Practice review slide 17.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Where is end-systole marked on the ECG?
options: At the beginning of the QRS complex
At the peak of the R wave
At the end of the T wave
questions.explanation: End-systole coincides with aortic valve closure, occurring around the end of the T wave (completion of ventricular repolarization). *(Practice review slide 19.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What does A represent in this M-mode image?
questions.explanation: The single central line where the cusps coapt during diastole is the aortic valve closure line. *(Practice review slide 21.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What does B represent in this M-mode image?
questions.explanation: The cusp that swings anteriorly (upward) to form the top edge of the systolic box is the right coronary cusp. *(Practice review slide 23.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What does C represent in this M-mode image?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Aorta as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 25.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What does D represent in this M-mode image?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Non-coronary cusp as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 27.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  In the M-mode parasternal view at the level of the aortic valve, which direction does the anterior wall of the LA move during LA filling?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Anteriorly as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 29.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  In the M-mode parasternal view at the level of the aortic valve, which direction does the anterior wall of the LA move during LA emptying?
questions.explanation: During LA emptying (diastole, with the mitral valve open), the wall recoils posteriorly as atrial volume falls. *(Practice review slide 31.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  In the M-mode parasternal view at the level of the mitral valve, what shape does the anterior mitral valve leaflet represent?
questions.explanation: The anterior mitral leaflet inscribes the classic ‘M’, with the E and A peaks of early diastolic and atrial filling. *(Practice review slide 33.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  In the M-mode parasternal view at the level of the mitral valve, what shape does the posterior mitral valve leaflet represent?
questions.explanation: The posterior leaflet moves opposite the anterior leaflet, tracing a mirror-image ‘W’. *(Practice review slide 35.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What does fluttering of the mitral valve leaflets seen on an M-mode tracing represent?
questions.explanation: High-frequency DIASTOLIC fluttering of the anterior mitral leaflet is the classic M-mode sign of aortic regurgitation — the AR jet vibrates the leaflet. 37 *(Practice review slide 37.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  How is the aortic root measured?
options: At the end of the T wave
At the beginning of the QRS complex
questions.explanation: The classic ASE M-mode convention measures the aortic root leading-edge to leading-edge, at end-diastole. 39 *(Practice review slide 39.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  How is the left atrium measured?
options: At the beginning of the QRS complex
At the end of the T wave
questions.explanation: The LA antero-posterior dimension uses the same leading-edge-to-leading-edge convention, measured at end-systole when the LA is largest. . 41 *(Practice review slide 41.)*

questions.stem: During quality review of an adult echo study, the following point is discussed.  What does D represent in this M-mode image?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Non-coronary cusp as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 27.)*

questions.stem: During quality review of an adult echo study, the following point is discussed.  In the M-mode parasternal view at the level of the aortic valve, which direction does the anterior wall of the LA move during LA filling?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Anteriorly as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 29.)*

questions.stem: During quality review of an adult echo study, the following point is discussed.  In the M-mode parasternal view at the level of the aortic valve, which direction does the anterior wall of the LA move during LA emptying?
questions.explanation: During LA emptying (diastole, with the mitral valve open), the wall recoils posteriorly as atrial volume falls. *(Practice review slide 31.)*

questions.stem: During quality review of an adult echo study, the following point is discussed.  In the M-mode parasternal view at the level of the mitral valve, what shape does the anterior mitral valve leaflet represent?
questions.explanation: The anterior mitral leaflet inscribes the classic ‘M’, with the E and A peaks of early diastolic and atrial filling. *(Practice review slide 33.)*

questions.stem: During quality review of an adult echo study, the following point is discussed.  In the M-mode parasternal view at the level of the mitral valve, what shape does the posterior mitral valve leaflet represent?
questions.explanation: The posterior leaflet moves opposite the anterior leaflet, tracing a mirror-image ‘W’. *(Practice review slide 35.)*

questions.stem: During quality review of an adult echo study, the following point is discussed.  What does fluttering of the mitral valve leaflets seen on an M-mode tracing represent?
questions.explanation: High-frequency DIASTOLIC fluttering of the anterior mitral leaflet is the classic M-mode sign of aortic regurgitation — the AR jet vibrates the leaflet. 37 *(Practice review slide 37.)*

questions.stem: During quality review of an adult echo study, the following point is discussed.  How is the aortic root measured?
options: At the beginning of the QRS complex
At the end of the T wave
questions.explanation: The classic ASE M-mode convention measures the aortic root leading-edge to leading-edge, at end-diastole. 39 *(Practice review slide 39.)*

questions.stem: During quality review of an adult echo study, the following point is discussed.  How is the left atrium measured?
options: At the end of the T wave
At the beginning of the QRS complex
questions.explanation: The LA antero-posterior dimension uses the same leading-edge-to-leading-edge convention, measured at end-systole when the LA is largest. . 41 *(Practice review slide 41.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  M-mode was the first modality in echocardiography. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: M-mode (motion mode) was the earliest echocardiographic display, predating cross-sectional 2D imaging. Otto traces echo's origins to these single-line motion tracings. *(Practice review slide 3.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  What is the sampling rate of M-mode imaging?
questions.explanation: M-mode interrogates a single scan line, so pulses aren't shared across a sector. Sampling reaches roughly 1000–2000 frames/s (≈1800), giving outstanding temporal resolution. *(Practice review slide 5.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  M-mode is the gold standard for measurements. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: Current ASE/Otto guidance favours direct 2D (or 2D-guided) linear measurements. A fixed M-mode cursor often can't stay perpendicular to the walls, which overestimates dimensions. *(Practice review slide 7.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  What is a characteristic of M-mode imaging?
options: Gives a visual representation of the anatomy
questions.explanation: M-mode's hallmarks are outstanding temporal resolution and a narrow single-line ‘ice-pick’ sample — so both b and c are correct. *(Practice review slide 9.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  Time is represented on the y-axis. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: On an M-mode tracing, time runs along the horizontal X-axis; depth (distance from the transducer) is on the vertical Y-axis. *(Practice review slide 11.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  The cursor needs to be perpendicular to the structure of interest for best practice. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: Perpendicular insonation yields the truest dimension and the strongest specular reflection from walls and valves. *(Practice review slide 13.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  Sweep speed can be adjusted on M-mode imaging to adjust for clinical situations and heart rate. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: Sweep speed is an operator-adjustable control that spreads or compresses the trace to suit the patient's heart rate and the event being studied. *(Practice review slide 15.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  Where is end-diastole marked on the ECG?

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  Where is end-systole marked on the ECG?

questions.explanation: End-systole coincides with aortic valve closure, occurring around the end of the T wave (completion of ventricular repolarization). *(Practice review slide 19.)*

questions.explanation: On an M-mode tracing, time runs along the horizontal X-axis; depth (distance from the transducer) is on the vertical Y-axis. *(Practice review slide 11.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  The cursor needs to be perpendicular to the structure of interest for best practice. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: Perpendicular insonation yields the truest dimension and the strongest specular reflection from walls and valves. *(Practice review slide 13.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  Sweep speed can be adjusted on M-mode imaging to adjust for clinical situations and heart rate. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: Sweep speed is an operator-adjustable control that spreads or compresses the trace to suit the patient's heart rate and the event being studied. *(Practice review slide 15.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  Where is end-diastole marked on the ECG?
options: At the beginning of the QRS complex
At the peak of the R wave
At the end of the T wave
questions.explanation: By the classic M-mode convention, end-diastole is taken at the peak of the R wave — the onset of ventricular contraction, when the LV is maximally filled. *(Practice review slide 17.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  Where is end-systole marked on the ECG?
options: At the peak of the R wave
At the end of the T wave
At the beginning of the QRS complex
questions.explanation: End-systole coincides with aortic valve closure, occurring around the end of the T wave (completion of ventricular repolarization). *(Practice review slide 19.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  What does A represent in this M-mode image?
questions.explanation: The single central line where the cusps coapt during diastole is the aortic valve closure line. *(Practice review slide 21.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  What does B represent in this M-mode image?
questions.explanation: The cusp that swings anteriorly (upward) to form the top edge of the systolic box is the right coronary cusp. *(Practice review slide 23.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  What does C represent in this M-mode image?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Aorta as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 25.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  What does D represent in this M-mode image?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Non-coronary cusp as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 27.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  In the M-mode parasternal view at the level of the aortic valve, which direction does the anterior wall of the LA move during LA filling?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Anteriorly as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 29.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  In the M-mode parasternal view at the level of the aortic valve, which direction does the anterior wall of the LA move during LA emptying?
questions.explanation: During LA emptying (diastole, with the mitral valve open), the wall recoils posteriorly as atrial volume falls. *(Practice review slide 31.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  In the M-mode parasternal view at the level of the mitral valve, what shape does the anterior mitral valve leaflet represent?
questions.explanation: The anterior mitral leaflet inscribes the classic ‘M’, with the E and A peaks of early diastolic and atrial filling. *(Practice review slide 33.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  In the M-mode parasternal view at the level of the mitral valve, what shape does the posterior mitral valve leaflet represent?
questions.explanation: The posterior leaflet moves opposite the anterior leaflet, tracing a mirror-image ‘W’. *(Practice review slide 35.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  What does fluttering of the mitral valve leaflets seen on an M-mode tracing represent?
questions.explanation: High-frequency DIASTOLIC fluttering of the anterior mitral leaflet is the classic M-mode sign of aortic regurgitation — the AR jet vibrates the leaflet. 37 *(Practice review slide 37.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  How is the aortic root measured?
options: At the end of the T wave
At the beginning of the QRS complex
questions.explanation: The classic ASE M-mode convention measures the aortic root leading-edge to leading-edge, at end-diastole. 39 *(Practice review slide 39.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  How is the left atrium measured?
options: At the end of the T wave
At the beginning of the QRS complex
questions.explanation: The LA antero-posterior dimension uses the same leading-edge-to-leading-edge convention, measured at end-systole when the LA is largest. . 41 *(Practice review slide 41.)*
